methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 1 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.0x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Substrate is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by James and Oliver Proud. The valuation assessment draws on a universe of 11 total comparables: 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage competitors including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor. The company has raised $100M+ to date.

Only one valuation method proved applicable given data constraints. Stage-progression analysis, using the $100M total raised as a base proxy, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement to subsequent funding rounds, yielding an implied valuation of $200M. Peer-median comparison cannot be applied: while 12 same-sector peers exist, filtering for identical stage, adjacent stage, and comparable valuation tier produced fewer than the three datapoints required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring is similarly inapplicable because Substrate's revenue is not on file—a standard limitation for private companies—and applying the 21.0x P/S median observed across public semiconductor peers would be methodologically unsound without a revenue figure.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $170M to $230M, centered on $200M. This range reflects high uncertainty: reliance on a single method, absence of direct peer multiples, and lack of revenue visibility constrain confidence. Key unknowns include Substrate's revenue run rate, gross margins, and customer concentration—each material to refined valuation under alternative methodologies.
